section_summary: This section details Japanese internal and foreign political developments from August 1940 to October 1941, focusing on the composition and shifting personnel of the Second and Third Konoye Cabinets. Major topics include the formal creation of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau under Imperial Ordinance No. 846 to centralize propaganda and censorship, and an analysis of the 'Jushin' (senior statesmen) council replacing the Genro. The records also cover diplomatic tensions, cabinet reshuffles, and the August 1941 attempted assassination of Minister without Portfolio Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma.

subfiles.about: An editorial analyzing Japanese military aggression, the southward advance, and the puppet regime of Wang Ching-wei.
subfiles.from: Chung Hwa Jih Pao / Chinese press
subfiles.summary: Translated Chinese commentary arguing that Japan, bogged down in China, cannot expand southward, that talks with Wang Ching-wei are futile, and that peace requires Japanese withdrawal.
subfiles.title: Chinese Press Commentary on Japan's Southward Expansion and the Wang Ching-wei Regime

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting new cabinet appointments made by the Emperor on September 28, 1940.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports the appointment of three new cabinet ministers by the Emperor on September 28, 1940. The appointees include Gotaro Ogawa as Minister of Railways, Kiyoshi Akita as Minister for Overseas Affairs, and Tsuneo Kanemitsu as Minister of Welfare.
subfiles.title: Appointment of New Cabinet Members

subfiles.about: An intelligence report analyzing the composition, long-range objectives, and military orientation of the Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith-Hutton, Lt.-Cmdr., U.S. Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Smith-Hutton describes the Second Konoye Cabinet of July 22, 1940 as Army-backed to build a fascist defense state, with Manchukuo-experienced personnel and serious economic vulnerabilities.
subfiles.title: Second Konoye Cabinet: Political Parties and Principal Leaders

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting an analytical summary of the proposed organization and functions of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew outlines the preliminary plans to establish a centralized Cabinet Intelligence Bureau superseding the existing office. The report includes an internal State Department summary sheet and identifies the ten-man drafting committee and proposed five divisions. Grew concludes that consolidating censorship and propaganda functions under a Director General of ministerial rank marks a significant step toward an authoritarian state structure.
subfiles.title: Organization of a New Cabinet Intelligence Bureau

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting press speculation on imminent cabinet changes, tripartite commissions, and the Batavia oil negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Grew relays press reports of an anticipated wartime cabinet reshuffle, tripartite technical commissions, Kobayashi's statements on Batavia petroleum talks, and American submarine parts in Hong Kong.
subfiles.title: Press Reports on Cabinet Changes, Tripartite Commissions, and Batavia Negotiations

subfiles.about: A military intelligence report providing biographical sketches of the ministers in the Second Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Lt. Col., Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Lieutenant Colonel Creswell submits biographical profiles of key ministers serving in the newly organized Second Konoye Cabinet. The report covers Yosuke Matsuoka, Hideki Tojo, Zengo Yoshida, Isao Kawada, Eiji Yasui, Tadaatsu Ishiguro, Akira Kazami, Kunihiko Hashida, and Ichizo Kobayashi. The attaché assesses the political orientations of the ministers and the general view regarding their attitudes toward the European Axis powers.
subfiles.title: Biographical Notes on Members of the Second Konoye Cabinet

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting that Prime Minister Konoye does not contemplate a cabinet reorganization.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1097 (November 4, 1940): Konoye contemplates no cabinet reorganization.
subfiles.title: No Reorganization of Cabinet Contemplated by Prince Konoye

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indicating that the formation of the Konoye Cabinet discouraged hopes for improved Anglo-Japanese relations.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Singapore Despatch No. 923 (September 14, 1940): the Konoye Ministry dampened hopes of improved Anglo-Japanese relations.
subfiles.title: Formation of Konoye Ministry and Anglo-Japanese Relations

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording the appointments of Naoki Hoshino and Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma as Ministers without Portfolio.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1277 (December 4, 1940): Hoshino and Hiranuma named Ministers without Portfolio.
subfiles.title: Appointment of Hoshino and Hiranuma as Ministers without Portfolio

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet analyzing the political impact of Baron Hiranuma's entry into the cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1279 (December 5, 1940): effect of Hiranuma's appointment on domestic politics.
subfiles.title: Political Effect of Hiranuma's Cabinet Appointment

subfiles.about: A despatch and regulatory texts concerning the formal establishment of the unified Cabinet Intelligence Bureau.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports the formal establishment of the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau under Imperial Ordinance No. 846 and Cabinet regulations. The despatch includes translated ordinances detailing the Bureau's five functional divisions overseeing news control, international propaganda, censorship, and arts guidance. Grew notes that the Army and Navy retained independent press sections at Imperial Headquarters, indicating incomplete military trust in the civilian agency.
subfiles.title: Establishment of the Intelligence Bureau

subfiles.about: A State Department memorandum transmitting a copy of Despatch No. 5206 to the Federal Bureau of Investigation.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum sending the FBI a copy of Despatch No. 5206 on the Cabinet Intelligence Bureau, with copies to MID and ONI.
subfiles.title: Transmission of Despatch No. 5206 to the FBI

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting imminent cabinet changes expected in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1360 (December 21, 1940): expected Japanese cabinet personnel changes.
subfiles.title: Cabinet Changes Expected in Japan

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet concerning the postponement of cabinet changes in the Finance and Commerce ministries.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1384 (December 27, 1940): editorial reasons for postponing Finance and Commerce ministry changes.
subfiles.title: Postponement of Cabinet Changes in Commerce and Finance

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reporting the investiture of Takio Izawa as a Privy Councilor.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1377 (December 26, 1940): investiture of Takio Izawa as Privy Councilor.
subfiles.title: Investiture of Takio Izawa as Privy Councilor

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reviewing the likelihood of the cabinet falling or shifting its policy orientation.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1372 (December 24, 1940): no immediate fall of the Konoye Cabinet expected despite dissatisfaction.
subfiles.title: Outlook for the Fall of the Cabinet or Change in Orientation

subfiles.about: A despatch and cross-reference sheet analyzing the evolution of the Jushin (senior statesmen) council replacing the solitary Genro.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew analyzes the institutional replacement of the traditional Genro by a council of 'Jushin' (former prime ministers and imperial advisers) headed by the Lord Privy Seal. Drawing upon an article by Dr. C. H. Spinks, Grew details how political assassinations and military ascendancy ended party government and diminished Prince Saionji's personal authority. He emphasizes that the new council represents a permanent, conservative advisory mechanism aligned with reactionary political forces.
subfiles.title: Japan's New Genro

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting that Prince Konoye temporarily assumed the duties of Foreign Minister during Matsuoka's absence.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports an official note dated March 12, 1941, informing the diplomatic corps that Prime Minister Prince Konoye would temporarily assume the duties of Foreign Minister while Yosuke Matsuoka was abroad.
subfiles.title: Konoye Temporarily Assumes Duties of Foreign Minister

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet relaying a rumor that Foreign Minister Matsuoka would resign in favor of General Tatekawa.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 76 (January 16, 1941): rumor Matsuoka may resign and be replaced by Tatekawa.
subfiles.title: Rumored Resignation of Matsuoka

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet concerning unverified reports of a plot by army officers to overthrow the Japanese government.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 276 (February 21, 1941): uncertain reports of an army faction plot to overthrow the government.
subfiles.title: Reported Army Plot to Overthrow Government

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet regarding rumors of cabinet reorganization due to economic difficulties and policy dissatisfaction.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 390 (March 11, 1941): possible cabinet restructuring amid policy discontent and economic pressure.
subfiles.title: Possible Reorganization of Cabinet Due to Policy Discontent

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet on the reorganization of the Imperial Rule Assistance Association and General Yanagawa's new role.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 472 (March 27, 1941): Yanagawa expected to become IRAA Vice President and Minister without Portfolio.
subfiles.title: Reorganization of Imperial Rule Assistance Association

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet announcing the appointments of Admiral Toyoda and General Suzuki to the cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 506 (April 4, 1941): Toyoda to Commerce and Industry, Suzuki to Planning Board.
subfiles.title: Appointments of Admiral Toyoda and General Suzuki

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reporting press reactions to Masatsune Ogura's appointment as Minister without Portfolio.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 495 (April 1, 1941): press comment on financier Masatsune Ogura's appointment as Minister without Portfolio.
subfiles.title: Press Comments on Appointment of Masatsune Ogura

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting favorable public and press reactions to the appointments of Toyoda and Suzuki.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 512 (April 5, 1941): favorable press comment on the Toyoda and Suzuki appointments.
subfiles.title: Favorable Press Comment on Toyoda and Suzuki Appointments

subfiles.about: A telegram stating that Prince Konoye declined to receive foreign diplomats and directed them to Vice Minister Ohashi.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports Konoye declined to receive him or the British Ambassador, referring them to Vice Minister Ohashi, in contrast to Roosevelt's accessibility to Ambassador Nomura.
subfiles.title: Konoye Declines Interview with Foreign Diplomats

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet summarizing Prime Minister Konoye's third formal press conference.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 524 (April 10, 1941): press summary of Konoye's third press conference as premier.
subfiles.title: Summary of Prime Minister Konoye's Press Conference

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting that Yosuke Matsuoka resumed his duties as Foreign Minister following his trip abroad.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew informs the Department of State that a diplomatic circular dated April 22, 1941, announced that Yosuke Matsuoka had resumed his official duties as Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.title: Matsuoka Resumes Duties as Foreign Minister

subfiles.about: Correspondence transmitting Australian diplomatic insights on conservative cabinet and IRAA appointments in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Australian Minister Casey sends Hornbeck Sir John Latham's view that the Ogura, Yanagawa and Ishiwata appointments show financial conservatives beating radicals, though instability is possible; Hornbeck acknowledges.
subfiles.title: Australian Legation Views on Japanese Cabinet Changes

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reporting the resignation of Agriculture Minister Tadaatsu Ishiguro and his replacement by Hiroyasu Ino.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1006 (June 11, 1941): Agriculture Minister Ishiguro resigns, succeeded by Ino.
subfiles.title: Resignation of Ishiguro and Succession of Ino

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reporting that Prince Konoye would head the reconstituted Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1019 (July 17, 1941): Konoye selected to head the Third Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Prince Konoye to Form New Cabinet

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet transmitting the membership list of the newly formed Third Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1029 (July 18, 1941): official roster of the Third Konoye Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Personnel of the New Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting that incoming Foreign Minister Admiral Toyoda scheduled initial introductory meetings with foreign envoys.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that the new Foreign Minister, Admiral Teijiro Toyoda, would receive diplomatic chiefs of mission individually on July 25, 1941. Grew notes that these pro forma meetings would be brief but offered an avenue to raise urgent questions if necessary.
subfiles.title: Foreign Minister Toyoda to Receive Chiefs of Mission

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet noting resignations submitted by Ambassador Honda and Vice Minister Ohashi.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1033 (July 19, 1941): resignations of Ambassador Honda and Vice Minister Ohashi after the cabinet change.
subfiles.title: Resignations of Ambassador Honda and Vice Minister Ohashi

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting the attempted assassination of Minister without Portfolio Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports that Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma was shot in the neck at his Tokyo residence by 33-year-old Naohiko Ishiyama. The Home Ministry announced that Hiranuma's wounds were not critical, while American news agencies filed rush bulletins.
subfiles.title: Attempted Assassination of Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma

subfiles.about: A confidential telegram reporting that Hiranuma was attacked because of his efforts to improve Japanese-American relations.
subfiles.summary: Grew relays that Hiranuma's assailant belonged to the nationalist Mitsubi-kai and was motivated by resentment of Hiranuma's efforts toward understanding with the United States.
subfiles.title: Motive for the Attack on Baron Hiranuma

subfiles.about: A telegram summarizing Japanese newspaper editorials on the attempted assassination of Baron Hiranuma.
subfiles.summary: Grew summarizes Tokyo editorials on the Hiranuma shooting: Nichi Nichi and Asahi deplore violence in a crisis, Kokumin condemns terrorism, and Chugai warns it shows internal dissension abroad.
subfiles.title: Editorial Reaction to the Attempted Assassination of Hiranuma

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet recording the appointment of Eiji Amau as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1248 (August 15, 1941): Eiji Amau appointed Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.title: Appointment of Eiji Amau as Foreign Vice Minister

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet concerning comments by the Japanese Ambassador in Washington regarding Admiral Toyoda and Baron Hiranuma.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 412 (July 19, 1941): Ambassador Nomura's comments on the cabinet, Toyoda and Hiranuma.
subfiles.title: Japanese Ambassador's Comments on Cabinet Appointments

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing a strictly confidential telegram regarding Prince Konoye's resignation and the formation of a new cabinet.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1646 (October 17, 1941): Konoye's resignation and formation of the Tojo Cabinet.
subfiles.title: Resignation of Prince Konoye and Formation of New Cabinet

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reporting German dissatisfaction with Matsuoka due to his verbosity and the Soviet neutrality pact.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1084 (July 25, 1941): German authorities favor Matsuoka's removal for his talkativeness and the Neutrality Pact.
subfiles.title: German Desire for the Removal of Matsuoka

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet reporting the appointment of Michiyo Iwamura as Minister of Justice.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Telegram No. 1086 (July 25, 1941): Michiyo Iwamura appointed Justice Minister.
subfiles.title: Appointment of Michiyo Iwamura as Justice Minister

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing a State Department memorandum on discussions regarding the new cabinet's composition.
subfiles.from: William Schmidt, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a July 16, 1941 memorandum of William Schmidt's talk with a Japanese Embassy secretary on the new cabinet.
subfiles.title: Discussions on the Composition of the Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: A cross-reference sheet indexing an analysis of current changes in the Japanese cabinet.
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Langdon's July 18, 1941 Far Eastern Affairs analysis of the Tokyo ministerial reorganization.
subfiles.title: Analysis of Current Changes in the Japanese Cabinet
